title: David Parnas and the Case for Information Hiding (1972)
explainer: The practice of splitting a program into modules by what each one hides, rather than by the order of its steps, traces back to David Parnas's influential 1972 paper "On the Criteria to Be Used in Decomposing Systems into Modules." Parnas argued each module should hide a design decision likely to change, so that other modules stay unaffected when it does, which is the real reasoning behind good file and module boundaries, not simply keeping files small.
